title: GDScript exported typed array retains old data when type is changed, causing error.
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5.1.stable.official

### System information

Linux 6.18.3-2-cachyos

### Issue description

When creating an exported property of an array of type in a gdscript, such as below:
```gdscript
@export var fu_bar: Array[int]
```
Then changing the type (e.g. [int] to [String]) after already populating the property in the inspector, trying to change the values in the inspector will cause an error, such as:
```
  ERROR: Attempted to set a variable of type 'String' into a TypedArray of type 'int'.
  ERROR: core/variant/array.cpp:511 - Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "set")" is true.
```
Notably, it appears the original data is retained and tries to be converted (A possible QoL feature?). If you change the type back, the original values are restored. If you change it to a convertible type, such as Array[int] to Array[String] (Instead of like, Array[int] to Array[Vector2]), it will successfully convert the existing specified values, but throw an error on change attempts.

The workaround is simply to clear out the array in the inspector, then repopulate it.

### Steps to reproduce

**Issue Steps:**
1. Create any Node (I'll be use an AnimatedSprite2D, but it doesn't matter.)
2. Attach a script with an exported array of type property, such as below:
```gdscript
extends AnimatedSprite2D

@export var fu_bar: Array[int]
```
3. Save the script to update the node.
4. Select the node.
5. In the inspector, populate the exported array property with any values (Such as setting the size to 3, and values of 1, 2, and 3)
6. Modify the script to change the array's type:
```gdscript
extends AnimatedSprite2D

@export var fu_bar: Array[String]
```
7. Save the script to update it.
8. Attempt to change the values of the property in the inspector, it will throw an error:
```
  ERROR: Attempted to set a variable of type 'String' into a TypedArray of type 'int'.
  ERROR: core/variant/array.cpp:511 - Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "set")" is true.
```
With this example, you'll see that the values of 1, 2, and 3 are retained and shown in the inspector, presumably converted to strings, but are unable to be modified. Changing the array type back to its original will allow you to edit the property as expected.

**Workaround Steps:**
1. Set the "Size" of the array property in the inspector to 0
2. Repopulate as you want, it'll work fine.

N/A
